meta.source: Coded from the published QP and mark scheme (4MA1_1H_2306). Derived metadata only. No exam question text transcribed.

coding_notes: CROSSOVER BLOCK: 1F q16-q24 = 1H q1-q9, nine questions worth 41 MARKS — the first series where the block is not exactly 40. Six consecutive pairs came to 40, which made it look like a rule; it is an observation. Verified by reading q16 against q1 rather than trusting the arithmetic.

GAP-CANDIDATE differentiation — q11(a), 2 marks, 'find dy/dx' for a cubic. UNTAGGED: nothing in data/skills.ts covers any part of differentiating. FIFTH sighting. q11(b), the x coordinates where the gradient takes a given value, is tagged solving_quadratic_equations_factorising as an interim measure, consistent with Jun24 1H q18 and Nov23 1H q16.

GAP-CANDIDATE arithmetic_series_sum — q20, 6 marks: two facts about an arithmetic series are given and the number of terms summing to a third value is wanted. Tagged simultaneous_equations as an interim measure. FIFTH sighting.
GAP-CANDIDATE domain_and_range — q17(a), 1 mark. Tagged functions_notation as an interim measure. THIRD sighting.

q23 is a FRUSTUM of a square-based pyramid — the second sighting after Nov23 2H q23, and now tagged on the frustum node directly rather than worked around, since restoring it to the iGCSE courses was the right call.

q16 tagged counting_elements_in_sets across all three parts: a three-set Venn where the given condition is n(A union B) = 42 and two of the three answers are themselves n() of a set expression. Takes that skill to seven parts on the Higher slice.

q14 is the FIRST sighting of difference_of_two_squares — 50g squared minus 18 factorises as 2(5g-3)(5g+3). It had read as unexamined across fifteen papers, which was Bucket C: earlier DOTS work sat inside questions tagged on algebraic_fractions or factorising_quadratics.
